theory.title: Selectors & Specificity
theory.content:
Selector Types

CSS selectors target elements for styling. They range from simple element/class/ID selectors to complex attribute and pseudo-class selectors.

/* Basic selectors */
p { color: black; }          /* element */
.btn { padding: 8px; }       /* class */
#header { height: 60px; }    /* ID */

/* Attribute selectors */
input[type='text'] { border: 1px solid #ccc; }
a[href^='https'] { color: green; }   /* starts with */
img[src$='.svg'] { width: 24px; }    /* ends with */

/* Combinators */
.nav > li { display: inline; }     /* direct child */
h2 + p { margin-top: 0; }          /* adjacent sibling */
h2 ~ p { color: #666; }            /* general sibling */

/* Pseudo-classes */
a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }
li:first-child { font-weight: bold; }
tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f5f5f5; }
input:focus { outline: 2px solid blue; }

Specificity Calculation

Specificity is a weight (A, B, C, D) that determines which rule wins when multiple rules target the same element:

  • A = 1 — inline style (style="...")
  • B = 1 — per ID selector (#id)
  • C = 1 — per class, attribute, or pseudo-class
  • D = 1 — per element or pseudo-element
p                    /* (0,0,0,1) */
.btn                 /* (0,0,1,0) */
#header              /* (0,1,0,0) */
#header .nav li      /* (0,1,1,1) */

/* !important overrides ALL — avoid except for utilities */
.u-hidden { display: none !important; }

The Cascade

When specificity is equal, the last rule in source order wins. Browser default styles (user-agent stylesheet) have the lowest priority; author styles override them.

theory.title: Box Model
theory.content:
How the Box Model Works

Every HTML element is rendered as a rectangular box composed of four areas: content → padding → border → margin (inside out).

/* Default: content-box — width/height applies to content only */
.box {
  width: 200px;
  padding: 20px;
  border: 2px solid black;
  margin: 16px;
  /* actual rendered width: 200 + 40 + 4 = 244px */
}

/* border-box — width/height includes padding + border */
* {
  box-sizing: border-box; /* recommended global reset */
}
.box {
  width: 200px;
  padding: 20px;
  border: 2px solid black;
  /* rendered width stays 200px — content shrinks */
}

Margins & Collapsing

Vertical margins between adjacent block elements collapse — the resulting margin equals the larger of the two, not their sum.

/* These two paragraphs get 24px gap, not 16+24=40px */
p { margin-bottom: 16px; }
p.large { margin-top: 24px; }

Display Types & the Box

  • block — takes full width, stacks vertically, respects all box model properties
  • inline — flows with text; top/bottom margin and height ignored
  • inline-block — flows inline but respects all box model properties
  • none — removes element from layout entirely (no space reserved)

theory.title: Flexbox
theory.content:
Flex Container

Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout model. Setting display: flex on a container makes its direct children flex items.

.container {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: row;         /* row (default) | column | row-reverse */
  justify-content: space-between; /* main axis alignment */
  align-items: center;         /* cross axis alignment */
  flex-wrap: wrap;             /* allow items to wrap */
  gap: 16px;                   /* spacing between items */
}

/* justify-content values */
/* flex-start | flex-end | center | space-between | space-around | space-evenly */

/* align-items values */
/* stretch (default) | flex-start | flex-end | center | baseline */

Flex Items

.item {
  flex: 1;           /* shorthand: flex-grow flex-shrink flex-basis */
                     /* flex: 1 = grow:1 shrink:1 basis:0% */
  flex-shrink: 0;    /* prevent shrinking below basis */
  align-self: flex-start; /* override container's align-items for this item */
  order: -1;         /* reorder without changing HTML */
}

/* Common patterns */
.spacer { flex: 1; }          /* pushes siblings apart */
.fixed { flex: 0 0 200px; }   /* fixed 200px, never grow/shrink */
.fluid { flex: 1 1 0; }       /* share remaining space equally */

Practical Patterns

  • Centered content: display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center
  • Sticky footer: page container min-height:100vh; flex-direction:column, main gets flex:1
  • Navigation bar: logo on left, links in center/right using spacer technique

theory.title: CSS Grid
theory.content:
Grid Container

CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system. It lets you define both rows and columns and place items precisely.

.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr;     /* 3 columns */
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;       /* 3 rows */
  gap: 16px 24px;                          /* row-gap column-gap */
}

/* Useful functions */
grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);    /* 3 equal columns */
grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr)); /* responsive */
grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr;         /* sidebar + content */

Placing Items

.header {
  grid-column: 1 / -1;   /* span all columns (start to end) */
  grid-row: 1;           /* first row */
}

.sidebar {
  grid-column: 1;        /* first column */
  grid-row: 2 / 4;       /* span rows 2-3 */
}

/* Named areas — more readable */
.layout {
  grid-template-areas:
    'header header'
    'sidebar main'
    'footer footer';
}
.header { grid-area: header; }
.sidebar { grid-area: sidebar; }
.main { grid-area: main; }

Grid vs Flexbox

  • Grid: 2D (rows AND columns), explicit placement, page-level layouts
  • Flexbox: 1D (row OR column), content-driven sizing, component-level layouts
  • Often used together: Grid for page layout, Flex for nav/card internals

theory.title: Responsive Design
theory.content:
Mobile-First Approach

Start with base styles targeting small screens, then progressively enhance for larger screens using min-width media queries. This produces smaller CSS for mobile and makes overrides easier.

/* Base: mobile */
.card { padding: 12px; font-size: 14px; }

/* Tablet */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .card { padding: 20px; font-size: 16px; }
}

/* Desktop */
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .card { padding: 32px; font-size: 18px; }
}

Common Breakpoints

  • 480px — large phones (landscape)
  • 768px — tablets
  • 1024px — small desktops / laptops
  • 1280px — standard desktops
  • 1536px — large screens

Fluid Units

/* Relative units */
font-size: 1rem;          /* relative to root font-size (16px) */
padding: 1em;             /* relative to element's font-size */
width: 100%;              /* relative to parent */
height: 100vh;            /* viewport height */

/* Clamp: fluid sizing between min and max */
font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.5rem);
width: clamp(200px, 50%, 800px);

Responsive Images

img {
  max-width: 100%;
  height: auto; /* preserve aspect ratio */
}

/* Art direction with picture element */

theory.title: Animations & Transitions
theory.content:
Transitions

Transitions smoothly animate a CSS property change from one state to another when triggered (e.g., on hover).

.btn {
  background: blue;
  transition: background 0.3s ease, transform 0.2s ease;
}
.btn:hover {
  background: darkblue;
  transform: translateY(-2px);
}

/* Syntax: property duration timing-function delay */
transition: all 0.3s ease-in-out;
transition: opacity 0.5s linear 0.1s; /* 0.1s delay */

Keyframe Animations

For complex multi-step animations, use @keyframes:

@keyframes slideIn {
  from { transform: translateX(-100%); opacity: 0; }
  to   { transform: translateX(0);     opacity: 1; }
}

@keyframes pulse {
  0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
  50%       { transform: scale(1.05); }
}

.modal {
  animation: slideIn 0.4s ease-out both;
}
.badge {
  animation: pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite;
}

Performance — GPU-Accelerated Properties

For smooth 60fps animations, only animate properties that the compositor can handle without triggering layout or paint:

  • transform — translate, scale, rotate, skew
  • opacity — fade in/out

Avoid animating width, height, top, left, margin — these trigger layout recalculation (reflow).

/* Good — GPU composited */
.moving { transition: transform 0.3s ease; }

/* Bad — triggers layout */
.moving { transition: width 0.3s ease; } /* avoid */

theory.title: CSS Custom Properties (Variables)
theory.content:
Defining & Using Variables

CSS Custom Properties (variables) cascade like regular properties and enable systematic design tokens and runtime theming.

/* Define on :root for global scope */
:root {
  --color-primary: #3b82f6;
  --color-bg: #ffffff;
  --spacing-md: 16px;
  --font-base: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  --radius: 8px;
}

/* Use with var() */
.btn {
  background: var(--color-primary);
  padding: var(--spacing-md);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  font-family: var(--font-base);
}

/* Fallback value */
color: var(--color-accent, #f59e0b);

Scoped Variables & Theming

/* Scoped to component */
.card {
  --card-padding: 24px;
  padding: var(--card-padding);
}

/* Dark mode theme */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --color-bg: #0f172a;
    --color-text: #e2e8f0;
  }
}

/* Theme class toggle (JS-controlled) */
.theme-dark {
  --color-bg: #0f172a;
  --color-text: #f8fafc;
}

Dynamic Updates with JavaScript

// Read a variable
getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)
  .getPropertyValue('--color-primary').trim();

// Update a variable at runtime
document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--color-primary', '#ef4444');

// Per-element theming
card.style.setProperty('--card-bg', userColor);
